tx:
Cinder cores have primary utility in situations where a player has more bonus experience than they need to reach a level or experience goal. The general formula for maximum useful bonus experience - that is, how much bonus experience is needed to reach a particular experience amount without having any bonus experience left over - is given by bxp = \tfrac{1}{2}\ exp, where \text{bxp} is bonus experience and \text{exp} is total experience needed. 
When a player has less than half their total experience needed in bonus experience, bxp < \tfrac{1}{2}\ exp, cinder cores will deplete a player's supply of bonus experience more quickly, but will not affect the total number of actions necessary to reach a total experience goal. When bxp > \tfrac{1}{2}\ exp, cinder cores will reduce total necessary actions, as they allow more bonus experience to be used per action. Concretely, an action that gives 100 base experience will normally use 100 bonus experience for a total experience gain of 200, but an equipped cinder core increases the bonus experience used to 250 for a total experience gain of 350. 
If a player is able to use cinder cores to completely exhaust their bonus experience, the formula bxp = \tfrac{5}{7}\ exp gives a more accurate estimate of maximum useful bonus experience. In addition, a player can expect to do 1-\tfrac{5}{7}=\tfrac{2}{7} of the total actions to reach their goal. 
Note that this is only an estimate: because cinder cores give an additional bonus experience burn rate after exploding, and because the additional buff can be gained from other players, the maximum possible bonus experience burn rate is 250%(100% + 10%) = 275%, which gives an upper bound of bxp = \tfrac{11}{15}\ exp.…
